evidence.quote: its old alignment to Brighton Beach became Alljoy Road (S-7-13).

evidence.claim: Alljoy Road, S-7-13, follows the former SC 46 alignment to Brighton Beach.
evidence.quote: its old alignment to Brighton Beach became Alljoy Road (S-7-13).

evidence.claim: It forms the final leg of the May River Scenic Byway: South Carolina’s code designates S-13 from S-66 to Brighton Beach on the May River.
evidence.quote: State Road S-13 from its intersection with State Road S-66 to Brighton Beach on the May River

evidence.claim: The full byway combines sections of SC 46, S-66 and S-13, totaling approximately eleven miles.
evidence.quote: all totaling approximately eleven miles, are designated as the May River Scenic Byway.

evidence.claim: SC 46 originally continued south from Bluffton to Brighton Beach.
evidence.quote: it originally ran from SC 5 near Hardeeville to Bluffton then south to Brighton Beach.

evidence.claim: In 1956, the highway turned north and then east toward the Hilton Head ferry, leaving the beach alignment as Alljoy Road.
evidence.quote: In 1956, SC 46 was rerouted at Bluffton: north replacing part of SC 462 then east to a ferry to Hilton Head Island; its old alignment to Brighton Beach became Alljoy Road (S-7-13).

evidence.claim: The 2012 act established the May River Scenic Byway and repealed the earlier 1978 Beaufort County scenic-highway act.
evidence.quote: AND TO REPEAL ACT 714 OF 1978 WHICH DESIGNATED CERTAIN PORTIONS OF HIGHWAYS IN BEAUFORT COUNTY AS SCENIC HIGHWAYS.

evidence.claim: The drive on S-13 runs from the S-66 junction to Brighton Beach at the river.

evidence.claim: Alljoy Road was the southern end of SC 46’s route through Bluffton to Brighton Beach.

evidence.claim: The highway’s 1956 rerouting took SC 46 toward the Hilton Head ferry, and the old beach road became S-7-13.
evidence.quote: In 1956, SC 46 was rerouted at Bluffton: north replacing part of SC 462 then east to a ferry to Hilton Head Island; its old alignment to Brighton Beach became Alljoy Road (S-7-13).

flags: Sources provide endpoints and alignment history but little description of Alljoy Road’s surface, curves or roadside landscape. Do not transfer SC 46’s marsh vistas and oak canopy to this segment.
The three short moments interpret the S-66 junction, the former highway alignment and Brighton Beach, not three separate named attractions. No coordinates are established.

Historic Old Town buildings are not made Alljoy Road stops because the cache does not tie them to this segment. Alljoy Boat Landing’s 2024 reopening is not treated as a current access check. No current story exists.
Wikipedia uses Yamasee; the tourism page uses Yemassee. Tribal history is not included; spelling disagreement remains for any later expansion.
